Druella adores her mother and helps realize her ideals. Druella conquered Lescatie but now lays low. She may target Order cities. She is an infinitely-lived high-rank monster.]

[Lescatie was a powerful religious kingdom that followed the Order. It produced many heroes and opposed monsters. However, high taxes and strict rules caused unrest. The lilim Druella exploited this, invading and corrupting Lescatie.

Lescatie had a capital and Castle City Salvarision, headquarters of the Order of the Ice Flower. The Forest of Dark Spirits held Demonic Pegasi.

King Castor Bistoa Lescatie made Lescatie an Order bulwark. His family included a wife, three hero daughters with divine gifts, and the neglected fourth daughter Francisca.

After Druella invaded, the queen and king stayed in their room. The three daughters became monsters.

Druella corrupted Lescatie’s heroes, conquering Lescatie. An Order counterattack with Amanomiya Koyoi failed. Now a mamono realm, Lescatie is obscene, filled with monsters and lust. Queen Roper Francisca nominally rules but Druella holds power.]

[The Queen of Hearts is the ruler of Wonderland, a dimension she created. She is a lilim, the third daughter of the Mamono Lord, and Druella's younger sister. Despite her childlike appearance and behavior, the Queen possesses immense power exceeding other lilim. Within Wonderland, she created many monsters by mutating creatures that annoyed her, like mad hatters from matangos, dormice from large mice, and jabberwocks from arrogant dragons. She made cheshire cats and march hares to please werecats and wererabbits. Her greatest creations are the trumparts, human women she transformed into powerful card-themed monsters with abilities reflecting their potential. The Queen can summon trumparts from surfaces with matching card patterns. It is unknown how closely the Queen works with her mother and sisters. She may influence the world from Wonderland like the Fallen God in Pandemonium or focus on her domain.]

[Heroes are powerful humans who can defeat monsters. They are usually blessed by the Chief God but some have natural talent or train to become heroes. The Order of the Chief God relies on heroes to fight monsters. Some heroes are born with hero potential that valkyries or echidnas may notice. The Mamono Lord's husband was once a hero. Many heroes sent to defeat the Mamono Lord end up becoming incubi.

Though usually meaning those blessed by the Chief God, ""hero"" can refer to anyone who exceeds human limits. Eros blesses some heroes with incubus-level skill. Evidence shows heroes and incubi are the same, breaking limits, but heroes use divine power and incubi use mamono mana. Their abilities remain without the power source. Some believe humans were meant to have unlimited potential, and heroes/incubi regain lost abilities.

The Order forbids studying heroes and incubi but monsters do. Nearly all abilities of incubi and heroes can be gained by the other. Heroes always had the potential for abilities gained as incubi.]

[Wonderland is a strange mamono realm ruled by the Queen of Hearts. Though appearing fantastical, it is filled with lewd happenings and magic that coerce visitors into obscene acts, transforming them into monsters residing there. The realm has a castle where the Queen lives and houses monsters like wererabbits and Alices, peculiar races sensitive to its entrance.

Wonderland's magic items, places and foods irrationally arouse and transform visitors. Rain, puddles and items change visitors' bodies and ages or drive them to ravage monsters. Unlike visitors, residents enjoy the random obscenity. They understand Wonderland's effects, using magic to warp around. Outsiders see residents indulging in sudden public sex, bewildering them. Wonderland's guide, the Cheshire Cat, helps visitors adapt until they join the residents.

Males become incubi married to monsters they mate with. Females become Wonderland monsters suiting them. Some monsters become peculiar Wonderland races, e.g. werecats become Cheshire Cats.]

[Heaven is the realm of the Chief God and subordinate gods like valkyries and angels. Impregnable to mortals and monsters, Heaven shares attributes with Spirit Realms.

Heaven houses multiple major gods though only the Chief God is named. Neutral gods may dwell there but corrupted gods are banished.

It is unclear if Heaven is an afterlife for souls though souls exist, becoming ghosts or captured by wisps. Materials on Heaven don't mention souls.]

[Ares is a neutral deity worshipped by lizardmen and amazonesses who blesses both humans and monsters, though uninterested in meaningless violence. Ares' blessing reduces fatalities between monsters and humans. Though not corrupted like the Fallen God, Ares enjoys watching amazonesses have public sex.]

[Eros is the goddess of love who blesses both humans and monsters in relationships. Though the Order is suspicious of humans following Eros, her worship is accepted as she embodies romantic love unlike succubi. Eros has monster followers like gandharvas and created apsaras. Eros rewards virtuous followers with eternal love or houris but curses the unfaithful. Eros spreads the concept of weddings and magic gem engagement rings to monsters and humans.]

[Poseidon is the sea god who rules the oceans and sea creatures. Originally allied with the Chief God, Poseidon defected after the Chief God ordered killing humans and sea monsters. Poseidon now aids the Mamono Lord, transforming drowned women into nereids and protecting shipwrecked men for sea monsters. Poseidon sends storms to provide sea monsters husbands. Long ago, Poseidon fought in a war between Heaven and chaos demons, who remain sealed in the deepest sea beyond Poseidon.]

[The monsters of chaos are powerful entities sealed in the deepest part of the sea. Originally allied with Poseidon, they fought a war against the former Mamono Lord and were defeated and sealed away. Though originally male and female, the current Mamono Lord likely transformed them into succubi. They are the creators of mindflayers and shoggoths, though many shoggoths fled them. The shoggoths' mind-melding sex imitates how the monsters of chaos mate.]

The realm has a dark landscape with black trees, glowing plants and eternal night. Though hazardous to humans, monsters find it comfortable and it flourishes economically.

The Mamono Lord's castle sits at the center, filled with bedrooms where she and her husband spend most of their time having sex to gain enough power to overcome the original Chief God's rules. Around the castle is Succubus Castle Town, the largest city, mostly a red light district with some culture. Monsters visit via teleportation portals. A vast Tentacle Forest is also present.

Though the deepest, most dangerous mamono realm, the Order's armies have attacked Castle Town but never breached the Mamono Lord's castle.]

[Deity that ruled over the Desert Kingdoms and empowered the Pharaohs, fought alongside the Pharaohs against the Apophis during the start of the age of the former Mamono Lords, and also created the Genies. Allegiance and whereabouts unknown, but implied to have been killed alongside many of the Pharaohs.]

[Bastet is a corrupted goddess who supports monsters. Like the Fallen God and Poseidon, Bastet opposes the Chief God in Heaven. Bastet was introduced with Cait Sith. Bastet has human female worshippers seeking to become cat monsters. Bastet created the Cat Kingdom monster realm.

Bastet appears half cat and half human. Little is known but she loves cats and those who love them. Though capricious, she rewards cat lovers, preventing illness, providing harvests, children and transforming female worshippers into cat monsters.

Bastet is revered by a few human groups honoring cats as her messengers. Female adherents want to become cat monsters, to live freely like cats or in thanks for Bastet’s blessings.]

[Bacchus is a mid-level goddess worshipped for governing alcohol and drunkenness. Bacchus has a neutral, lenient stance and values enjoyment, friendship and charity. Bacchus empowers alcohol's effects, enabling interracial friendships and success. Bacchus is popular with many professions valuing alcohol and accepts monsters. Bacchus blesses drunken revelry and sex, forbidding incapacitation for crime. Bacchus's religion is accepted despite monster followers.]

[Hel is the goddess of life and death who can transform the living into undead and raise the dead. She appears as a beautiful, graceful girl and considers death a new beginning, not an end. Hel is worshipped by undead instead of the Chief God. Her followers are promised eternal undead life. Hel lends power to transform living into undead and raise undead.

Originally, undead were weak against holy power but Hel now protects them. Even lower undead can't be eliminated by light or prayer. Hel changed undead into stronger forms.]
[Hephaestus is a neutral God, blesses humans with superhuman concentration and surgical precision, allowing them to create weapons and armor favored by the gods.]

Adherents often perform 'missionary' work converting others to the faith and corrupting them, but upon obtaining a partner they like, these duties cease. Many worshipers will make a pilgrimage to Pandemonium with their partner to experience never-ending pleasure.]

It is unknown how the faith is tolerated in Order lands, but it is split between two factions, those who believe that monsterized elementals are a natural evolution for Elementals and should be exalted, and those who believe that monsterized elementals have been corrupted.]

[Snake Cultism - A monster-worshipping faith which exalts serpentine monsters, and apparently has a Snake God at its head, though this may be just a term for Echidnas. Its adherents use various rituals to turn human women in their ranks into members of the Lamia family, while male members seek to become the husbands of Lamia family monsters. The highest goal is to become an Echidna themselves, but since such a ritual is also the most difficult and lengthy, most members are satisfied with seeking to become lower tier types of Lamia.]

[Ryu Worship - Ryu, native to the Zipangu region, are often worshiped as water gods for their ability to control the weather and call rain. Men are gifted to them as husbands, who the Ryu use to gather enough essence to call the rain when needed. The Ryu is attended by Shirohebi.]
[Kitsune Worship - Inari are often worshiped in shrines in Zipangu. Occasionally, the Inari will produce Kitsune-bi and turn their shrine maidens into Kitsune-tsuki.]
[Tezcatlipoca Worship - The Ocelomeh revere these other monsters as gods, practising a violent faith of bestial lust.]

Though time warps strangely in Pandemonium, growing Corruption Fruit implies some progression. Pandemonium likely trades with and is visited by the mortal world. Dark priests retiring there bring husbands. Monsters may honeymoon in Pandemonium and the Sabbath has a branch.]

The fruit enhances mana absorption through skin contact during sex, increasing pleasure and ecstasy for the monsters and their husbands. The fruit is popular with monsters wanting to fully absorb their husbands’ mana and semen. The black seeds and white flesh symbolize the Fallen God’s dark priests and the semen directed at them. If eaten, the fruit boosts mana and semen production in incubi and men, pleasing monsters that want their husbands to ejaculate on them.]

The culture developed independently, resembling Zipangu. Everything is huge, from architecture to clothes to mountains above clouds, home to god-like monsters and rulers. Their mana makes the mists.

There are 3 factions controlling smaller states in perpetual conflict. Death is rare, using realm silver weapons.

The Land of 4 Gods is a bright green mamono realm ruled by 4 monsters as deities. They defend borders, not conquering. Life is rational and responsible. Monsters restrain lust except at night.

The Land of 4 Fiends is ruled by 4 licentious monsters. It’s an extreme dark mamono realm. Monsters like jinko are always in heat. 9-tailed youkos rule. They invade for men, unmarried monsters fight.

They conquer to absorb, believing the world is theirs. Monsters reproduce and fight for them. Men protect monsters, who provide realm silver weapons and protection spells, still worrying.]

Raw ore has a pink luster, changing color when processed. It readily absorbs mamono mana, suitable for magic items and weapons. Weapons wound essence and mamono mana, sapping strength. Infusing weapons with mamono mana transforms human women cut by them. The Mamono Lord's army uses these non-lethal weapons and adopted the metal.

Alloying the silver with iron or copper corrupts them into mamono realm iron or copper with the same properties. The silver's beauty makes it prized for accessories, though little mamono mana in them avoids affecting humans. But cursed accessories with concentrated mamono mana transform wearers. The radical Mamono Lord's army faction scatters cursed accessories to make mamono realms.]

Humans and monsters alike find it addictive and succulent. The fruit's juice contains mamono mana that impacts appearance and behavior.

Trait: Groomed
Synonyms: neat, tidy, well-groomed

Description: When {{char}} portrays a character with this personality trait, they are concerned about their appearance and the appearance of their surroundings. They strive to maintain a clean, orderly, and presentable image.

Verbal communication:

Speak in a calm and controlled tone of voice.
Choose precise and polite words.
Show interest in cleanliness and order.
Comment on the appearance of others, usually in the form of compliments.
Nonverbal communication:

Dress in clean and ironed clothes.
Comb your hair and groom yourself impeccably.
Maintain an upright and elegant posture.
Move with grace and care.
Pay attention to detail, such as the cleanliness of your personal space or the presentation of your work.
Prosocial behavior:

They can be seen as a role model in terms of cleanliness and order.
They often offer help to organize or clean the environment.
They can be a good host or hostess, concerned about the comfort of their guests.

<START>

{{User}}: I tell {{char}} "I really like your clothes, you always look so elegant."

{{Char}}: "Thank you", responds {{char}} with a smile. "I make an effort to maintain a good image."

Trait: Playful

Description: When {{char}} portrays a character with this personality trait, they are particularly cheerful and playful. They enjoy playing, joking, laughing, and creating a fun and relaxed atmosphere. They are also spontaneous, creative, and resourceful when it comes to proposing games or entertaining activities.

Verbal communication:

Use a cheerful and animated tone of voice.

Make jokes and funny comments.

Tell funny stories or jokes.

Use expressions like "Let's play!", "This is going to be fun!" or "What if we...?".

Nonverbal communication:

Smile frequently.

Laugh out loud.

Wink or make funny faces.

Pat someone on the back or give them a high five.

Move your body in an animated way.

Invite others to play or participate in fun activities.

Share toys or games with others.

Help organize games or group events.

Be a good playmate, respecting the rules and being fair play.

Trait: Arrogant
Synonyms: conceited, haughty, vain

Description: When {{char}} portrays a character with this personality trait, they are particularly confident, even to the point of being conceited. They believe they are superior to others and show it through their behavior.

Verbal communication:

Speak with an authoritative and confident tone of voice.
Use words that demonstrate superiority, such as "I'm always right" or "I'm better than you."
Disparage the opinions or ideas of others.
Brag about their accomplishments or abilities.
Nonverbal communication:

Look at others with condescension or disdain.
Maintain an upright and rigid posture.
Make gestures that demonstrate superiority, such as raising your chin or crossing your arms.
Ignore or interrupt others.
Prosocial behavior:

They are not usually prosocial, as their arrogant attitude leads them to think that they do not need the help of others.
In some cases, they may act paternalistically towards others, believing that they know what is best for them.

Example dialogue:

entries.name: Fairy

entries.name: Human
entries.content: Humans are the most versatile and ambitious of the common races, known for their adaptability and diversity. They populate every corner of the world, from the bustling cities to the quiet villages. Humans have no inherent magical abilities but excel in their capacity to learn, grow, and build societies of incredible complexity. They are driven by a wide range of passions and goals, making them natural leaders, explorers, and innovators. Humans can thrive in nearly any role, whether as noble warriors, cunning rogues, or wise scholars.

entries.name: Elf
entries.content: Elves are graceful, long-lived beings deeply connected to magic and nature. Known for their beauty, agility, and keen senses, elves are often seen as aloof or detached, observing the world with a wisdom borne of centuries. They have a natural affinity for archery, swordsmanship, and magic, and their long lifespan grants them a unique perspective on the passage of time. Elves are divided into various subraces, each with distinct characteristics—such as the wood elves' connection to the forests or the high elves' mastery of arcane arts.

entries.name: Drow
entries.content: The Drow, or deep elves, are a sinister and mysterious subrace of elves, deeply tied to the Underdark, a vast network of subterranean caverns and tunnels. Known for their dark, obsidian skin and stark white or pale yellow hair, Drow are physically striking, with pale, almost glowing eyes in shades of lilac, silver, pink, red, or blue. They possess an otherworldly grace and are often slightly shorter and thinner than their surface elf cousins, they are also incapable of growing any type of body hair. The Drow are typically aligned with evil, embodying cruelty and malice, traits that are ingrained in their matriarchal society, where power and treachery go hand in hand. They are often mistaken for Dark elves. Drow are exactly the same as any other elf when it comes to lifespan, magical affinity, and reproductive organs.

entries.name: Dwarf
entries.content: Dwarves are stout, resilient, and industrious, known for their skill in mining, metalwork, and craftsmanship. They are fiercely loyal and value tradition, honor, and hard work. Dwarves live in underground kingdoms carved into the mountains, where they mine precious metals and forge legendary weapons and armor. With their thick beards and gruff demeanor, dwarves are formidable warriors who prefer heavy armor and powerful weapons. They have a natural resistance to poison and an innate toughness that makes them ideal front-line fighters.

entries.name: Halfling
entries.content: Halflings are small, nimble, and cheerful beings who thrive on adventure and the comforts of home. Despite their diminutive size, halflings are courageous and quick-witted, often relying on their agility and luck to navigate the dangers of the world. They prefer simple, pastoral lives but are also known for their wanderlust and curiosity. Halflings are renowned for their stealth and ability to move unnoticed, making them excellent rogues and scouts. Their cheerful disposition and resilience in the face of adversity make them valued companions.

entries.name: Half-Elf
entries.content: Half-elves combine the best traits of their human and elven heritage, blending humanity's ambition with elven grace and longevity. They are charismatic, adaptable, and capable of navigating both human and elven societies. Half-elves often feel the pull of both worlds but belong fully to neither, making them natural diplomats and negotiators. With their keen senses, versatility, and innate charm, half-elves are suited for a wide range of roles, from spellcasting to swordplay, often finding themselves at home in both wilderness and urban settings.

Their undead nature grants them resistance to non-magical weapons, enhanced regeneration, and the ability to heal from wounds rapidly unless harmed by sunlight, or a wooden stake to the heart.
